newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Telecom denies ITJ acquisition report.
newsitem.headline: Japan Telecom denies ITJ acquisition report.

text.p: Japan Telecom Co Ltd denied a newspaper report on Thursday that said it was negotiating over a possible acquisition of International Telecom Japan Inc (ITJ).
"There is no such fact that we have reached an (acquisition) agreement and we are not negotiating (one)," a Japan Telecom spokesman said.

The Japanese daily Sankei Shimbun reported on Thursday that Japan Telecom, a long-distance telecommunications operator, and ITJ, which offers international telecommunications services, had agreed that Japan Telecom would acquire ITJ as early as October for 80 billion yen.

The Japan Telecom spokesman added, however: "It is true that officials of the two companies have held meetings since autumn 1995 to discuss possible ways, including the possibility of an alliance, to cope with changes in the telecommunications industry."

Earlier this week, Japan Telecom director Taro Sasaki told a news conference that the company was planning to launch international telecommunications services in the spring of 1998 by connecting its lines with those of Japanese international carriers.
He said that Japan Telecom was talking with three international carriers -- Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd, IDC Corp and ITJ -- about conditions for using each other's lines.
